summary: Uneven quota enforcement for subpath routes causing intermittent 429s during signed URL fan-out
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports intermittent 429s observed only during large import jobs that use signed upload URLs. The pattern is uneven: some files always succeed while others from the same job get rate limited. Impact: customer ingestion pipeline for product images stalls ~10-30% of files, causing downstream retry storms and timeouts in their processing queue. Environment: BrightCart on a Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-11) with inbound uploads routed through the signed-url service and an edge API gateway in us-east-1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a batch of 500 signed upload URLs from BrightCart UI. 2) Kick off 50 parallel worker processes (same host pool) to PUT files using signed URLs. 3) Observe successful 200s interleaved with 429s on a subset of PUT/POST calls. 4) Reduce parallelism to <8 workers and retries succeed without sustained 429s. Observed behavior: 429s appear within first 30s of a job and persist for several minutes. Throttled requests indicate tenant token exhaustion but the tenant quota dashboard shows credits still available. Temporary workaround: advise customer to stagger signed-url generation and reduce parallel PUT concurrency to 8-12 per host while we investigate.

investigation: Findings: 1) The signed-url generator emits URLs with embedded query parameters in non-deterministic order. 2) Our edge token-accounting layer uses the raw request path+query as the key for per-route token buckets in the short refill window. 3) For some PUT flows an upstream validation request (signed-url verification) was hitting a different route variant before the actual upload, causing the tenant quota to be decremented twice in quick succession. 4) NAT/pooled IP reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing further amplify observed bursts because multiple logical connections map to the same client token window. Evidence: correlated edge logs (edge-logs-us-east-2026-03-10.gz) show paired count decrements for request_ids supplied by the customer. Rate-limiter debug trace: rl.trace.833123 shows double-debit events when query param order differs. Hypothesis: lack of canonicalization for signed-url subpaths + preflight validation calls leads to uneven quota consumption and perceived early exhaustion.
resolution: Workaround implemented: edge normalization filter that canonicalizes query parameter order and strips non-accounting prefixes from signed URLs; customer advised to limit parallel PUTs and to batch signed-url issuance with a small splay. Permanent fix: engineering PR https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/7890 implements canonicalization in the token-accounting path and adds a de-duplication check for back-to-back validation+upload pairs. Rollout notes: feature gated and deployed to us-east canary on 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC, monitored for 24 hours. Post-deploy result: BrightCart reported reduction of 429s to baseline. Follow-ups: (1) run a quota backfill job to reconcile short-lived double-debits and issue credits to affected billing accounts, (2) add Console toggle and documentation page explaining signed-url counting semantics, (3) schedule a runbook update for support. Related PRs and runbooks listed in metadata. Ticket to be closed after backfill complete and docs published.
